clue.text: Afternoon's ruined, on leaving part of Brighton?

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order once the two named letters are set aside

parts.note: the possessive's S is kept as a letter here, giving the full run of ten letters
the word on is what leaves the mixed letters, as the clue says

explanation.surface: Someone's afternoon on the south coast has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' says ON drops out of the pool: the ten letters of AFTERNOONS, less O and N, are rearranged ('ruined'). Brighton is an English seaside resort, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a seaside town, and its promenade along the beach is one stretch of the coast road found there.

clue.text: Single maiden, disheartened, gloomy

parts.note: sole means single or only

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letters are dropped, leaving only the first and last

explanation.surface: An unmarried young woman, dispirited, is feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a cricket maiden (M); here the word itself loses its insides to give MN.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means serious and sombre, close in mood to gloomy.

clue.text: A mostly radical change to achieve rural paradise

indicators.note: a change rearranges the remaining letters into a new order
mostly means all but the end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A radical change is almost what is needed to reach a country idyll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter before 'change' rearranges what is left; 'to achieve' is a link. Arcadia is the poets' ideal countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of Greece, became the poets' name for an idyllic pastoral paradise.

clue.text: Book heavy metal band, perhaps, introduced by up-and-coming pro

indicators.note: introduced by means taken in by, so the band's letters go inside the reversed word
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a manacle is a heavy metal ring or band locked round the wrist

explanation.surface: A book about a heavy metal group, introduced by a rising professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal band' suggests a rock group but is a shackle. 'up-and-coming' reads the word for pro upwards (ROF), and 'introduced by' puts the shackle inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roman-à-clef is a novel in which real people appear thinly disguised as fictional characters.

clue.text: Say chess piece will inevitably be toppled in play

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the sound of the chess word counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: the knight is a chess piece
must expresses what will inevitably happen
to fall is to be toppled

explanation.surface: In a game of chess, a piece is bound to be knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: Night Must Fall is a 1935 thriller play by Emlyn Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Night Must Fall is a psychological thriller written for the stage by Emlyn Williams.

clue.text: Exotic food detailed in menu: such unusual mixture for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so each of the six words before this phrase gives up its opening letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant's menu promises an unusual mixed dish of foreign food.
explanation.walkthrough: The six words after the colon's lead-in ('detailed in menu: such unusual mixture') each give their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These Chinese dumplings and small steamed dishes are a cuisine many Western diners regard as foreign and unusual.

clue.text: Introductory part missing from quintets he composed

indicators.note: the introductory part is the first letter, which goes missing from the word for quintets

parts.note: a quintet is a group of five, so quintets are fives

explanation.surface: Quintets are missing their opening section, written by some composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer, so he is someone who composed.

clue.text: Extra money put in post as payment

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the word for posting

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is extra money given for service

explanation.surface: A bonus has been mailed as wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular sum paid, as to a clergyman or student.

clue.text: Air in shopping centre associated with illness

indicators.note: in places the tune inside the shopping word

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
an aria is an air, a song in opera

explanation.surface: The atmosphere in a shopping centre is linked to sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests the atmosphere; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarial means relating to malaria, the mosquito-borne disease.

clue.text: American state turned back thousands from India

indicators.note: turned back says the letters for the state are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Cal is a standard abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: An American state has rejected large sums arriving from India.
explanation.walkthrough: In India a lakh or lac is a hundred thousand, so the plural sense of 'thousands' is fair: it is a count of many thousands.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian numbering a lac (lakh) is one hundred thousand, a unit made of many thousands.

clue.text: Commanding soldiers to wear khaki, perhaps

indicators.note: the soldiers put the cloth on, so the cloth's letters go around theirs

parts.note: khaki is one example of a fabric, so a cloth word stands in for it
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are ordered to put on their khaki uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'khaki, perhaps' defines by example: khaki is one kind of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A magisterial manner is authoritative and imperious, the bearing of someone used to giving orders.

clue.text: Attempt to discredit a politician, caught by camera shot produced in evidence

indicators.note: produced in means set inside the word for evidence

parts.note: a sign is a piece of evidence, an indication

indicators.note: caught by means held within the scrambled camera letters
shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is caught on camera, and the footage is produced as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles the camera letters into MEARCA, which 'caught by' wraps round A MP just before its final letter; 'produced in' sets that whole run inside the evidence word.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear campaign is an organised effort to damage someone's reputation with damaging claims.

clue.text: Seamstresses making dress and overall: the reverse of matching garments

parts.note: a midi is a dress of mid-calf length
net means final, after everything, as in an overall or net figure

indicators.note: the reverse of says the following word's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a set is a group of matching items, such as a twinset of garments

explanation.surface: A fashion note about seamstresses making a dress and overall, in contrast with matching outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overall' looks like a garment beside 'dress', but it means final or total.
explanation.definitionFit: Midinettes are Parisian shop girls, especially young workers in the dressmaking and millinery trade.

clue.text: Sport makes you largely tired

indicators.note: largely means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: weary means tired

explanation.surface: Playing games leaves you worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is the verb: to sport a hat is to wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport something is to wear it showily, as when someone sports a bow tie.

clue.text: After several weeks on course I'll reach a part of Canada

parts.note: Nov is November, a month and so several weeks
Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire
the I of the contraction stands for itself

explanation.surface: A racehorse arrives in Canada after weeks at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse, famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's Atlantic maritime provinces.

clue.text: Member of Chinese family received by German church

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Member of Chinese family received by German church' (6), MANCHU: no parse found for how 'received by German church' builds the letters; CH for church is clear but the source of MAN and U is not.
annotationWithheld.clue: Member of Chinese family received by German church

clue.text: Right Honourable doctor of divinity based near a Welsh valley

parts.note: Hon is the abbreviation for Honourable, a courtesy title
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A titled clergyman with a divinity doctorate lives near a valley in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhondda is a former coal-mining valley in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a famous valley in South Wales, known for its coal-mining history.

clue.text: Magazine's mounting prejudice about north Africans

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means going up, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

indicators.note: about means around, so the prejudice word surrounds the letter

parts.note: bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: A magazine's growing bias against people from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: MAG read upwards gives GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambians are people of The Gambia, a West African country.

clue.text: Stop keeping minutes in support of chairperson?

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the stopping word goes around the other letter

parts.note: to arrest is to stop or halt

explanation.surface: A meeting is halted while the minutes are kept for the chairperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chairperson' suggests a committee chair; here it is anyone sitting in a chair, whose arm rests on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the part of a chair that supports the arm of whoever is sitting in it.

clue.text: Brand name on the bottom of the tent

parts.note: a marque is a brand name, especially of a car

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A brand name printed on the bottom of the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places MARQUE above the E in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and outdoor events.

clue.text: Indian quickly lassoes horse

indicators.note: a lasso encircles its catch, so the quick word goes round the letter for horse

parts.note: apace means quickly
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A Native American rider swiftly ropes a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, the sense of Indian in older usage.

clue.text: Irish copper wearing helmet reveals it? Yes and no

definitions.text: Irish copper wearing helmet reveals it? Yes and no

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the hat goes around the other letters

parts.note: a helmet is a kind of hat
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An Irish policeman's helmet covers up his trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman; it is the element. Taking off the helmet would show the trim, yet the cut lies in the hair, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut is the result of cutting the hair, which a helmet hides and its removal reveals.

clue.text: Fool gobbles up uncooked chicken

indicators.note: gobbles means swallows, so the fool word takes in the other

parts.note: to cod is to fool or hoax someone

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: A fool wolfs down some raw chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' is not poultry but a cowardly person. RAW read upwards gives WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a coward, someone lacking in courage.

clue.text: Poet refused entry by speaker

indicators.note: words given by a speaker are heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: barred means refused entry or excluded

explanation.surface: A poet is turned away at the door by the speaker of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially a traditional one reciting epic verse.

clue.text: Top composer's love for one type of coffee

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O in tennis scoring, and one is the Roman numeral I; the phrase puts the first in place of the second

parts.note: Puccini was an Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A leading composer's favourite drink is one kind of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The last I of PUCCINI becomes O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an espresso coffee topped with frothed milk, one of the familiar café varieties.

clue.text: Sea mist causing worry

definitions.meaning: a sea fog drifting inland from the North Sea coast

explanation.surface: Fog off the sea makes people anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Fret is a dialect word for coastal sea fog, and as a verb it means to worry.

clue.text: Painter with no heart for disagreement among group of celebs

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of, so the row goes inside the celebrity group

parts.note: the A-list is the set of top celebrities

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, which is removed

parts.note: a quarrel is a disagreement

explanation.surface: An artist feels no sympathy for squabbles among famous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heart' removes the middle R of the row word, leaving QUAREL; 'for' is a link, and 'among' places that inside the celebrity group.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarellist is a painter in watercolours, aquarelle being a watercolour technique.

clue.text: About to consume hot drink

indicators.note: consuming means taking something inside, so the word for about holds the other letter

parts.note: ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is about to have a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot drink' looks like the definition but 'hot' gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is British slang for tea, from the Chinese word for that drink.

clue.text: We stay out, affected by the heat

indicators.note: out signals that the preceding letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: We stay indoors because the weather is so hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sweaty is perspiring, which is how the body reacts to hot conditions.

clue.text: Redundant worker's stopped out of union

indicators.note: the worker plugs the gap, so it is placed inside the unmarried word

parts.note: unwed means unmarried, outside the union of marriage
an ant is the standard crossword worker; the 's here is short for has

explanation.surface: A redundant worker has stopped being a union member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union; it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is surplus to needs, which means nobody wants it any more.
